results.alertTitle: Multiple failed logon attempts against SOC-FW-RDP

summary.tpReason: Telemetry directly confirms the alert: 11,970 Windows 4625 failures against 257 accounts on SOC-FW-RDP in the stated one-hour window. The broad account list and NTLM use are consistent with password spraying/brute force, not a counting or rule artifact.
summary.fpReason: The telemetry lacks source IP and detailed 4625 failure status, so an authorized scanner or assessment cannot be completely excluded; however, the volume and 257-account spray pattern make benign activity unlikely.
summary.whatHappened: Between 2021-10-22 11:08:01Z and 12:07:39Z, SOC-FW-RDP recorded 11,970 failed logons (event 4625), using NTLM, against 257 distinct user-name strings. Heaviest targets were \\ADMINISTRATOR (9,997), \\ADMIN (503), \\USER (269), \\TEST (263), and \\SERVER (240). During 2021-10-22, the only 4624 successes on this host were 10 logons for NT AUTHORITY\\SYSTEM using Negotiate; no targeted account success was found. This supports a real password-spray/brute-force attempt with no evidence of successful authentication or compromise in available telemetry.
keyEvidence: SecurityEvent: 11,970 EventID 4625 records on SOC-FW-RDP from 2021-10-22 11:08:01.692Z through 12:07:39.740Z, targeting 257 accounts; all were User/NTLM/Security-channel events.
SecurityEvent account distribution: \\ADMINISTRATOR 9,997 failures; \\ADMIN 503; \\USER 269; \\TEST 263; \\SERVER 240, plus 252 other names.
SecurityEvent query for SOC-FW-RDP across 2021-10-22 found only 10 EventID 4624 successes, all NT AUTHORITY\\SYSTEM with Negotiate; no targeted-account success was observed.
No source IP or detailed failure-status fields were available in normalized SecurityEvent records, and no matching CommonSecurityLog records identified the origin.
summary.nextAction: Treat as a true-positive attack attempt, not a confirmed compromise. Identify the source via raw 4625 fields, RDP gateway, firewall, or flow logs and block/rate-limit it. Confirm the host is not unnecessarily internet-exposed; review targeted-account successes and process activity for 24 hours before/after, and reset/contain any account if a success is found. Check whether this was an approved scan.
